quotes_checked: 29 of 29 exact (all passages on the card, each read against the server; the partial-verse quotes are exact clauses)

fixes.why: The verse Lutheran and Reformed readers cite first for an inherited condition, Ephesians 2:3, is absent, and Romans 5:12 (their other main text for original sin) stands only under reading 1, so the card reads as though inherited sin were a Catholic and Orthodox matter. Reading 2 also has no verse for the condition from birth apart from Psalm 51:5.
fixes.fix: Replace Jeremiah 17:9 (carried also by Genesis 6:5 and Psalm 51:5 on the heart) or add Ephesians 2:3: "All of us also lived among them at one time, fulfilling the cravings of our flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts. Like the rest, we were by nature children of wrath." Note: "Read as naming a condition belonging to people by nature, apart from their own acts." If a ninth is not wanted, keep the count at eight by swapping Jeremiah 17:9 out. Also add to reading 2's answers: "They read Romans 5:12-19 with Ephesians 2:3 as naming a condition passed from Adam to all."

fixes.why: Reading 1 names synergy and a will that answers grace, but has no verse on the will or on working with God, while the verses cited by Orthodox readers for synergy are standard. Its passages are almost all about the image, conscience and Adam, so the card shows reading 1 less in its holders' own proof texts than readings 2 and 3.
fixes.fix: Swap Luke 10:30 (see next item) or 1 Corinthians 15:22 for 1 Corinthians 3:9: "For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field, God's building." Note: "Read by Orthodox readers as naming human beings who work together with God." Revelation 3:20 ("Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me.") is the alternative, and Wesleyan readers cite it as well.

fixes.why: The parable is a story told in answer to 'who is my neighbor', and the traveler as humankind is an allegorical reading by early Christian writers, not something the verse says. The note should say it is that reading, and it should not read as the verse's own point. The _why asks whether 'Early Christian readers' is old enough to say without a name: it is, since the allegory is widely attested among the church fathers, so the claim can stand.
fixes.fix: "Early Christian writers read the traveler left half dead allegorically, as humankind wounded and not dead; this is their reading of the parable and not its stated point."

fixes.why: Psalm 51:5 sits under reading 2 and nothing says how the other readings take it. The _why notes the gap. Literary readers also note it is Hebrew poetic self-accusation in a penitential psalm, which the other readings take differently.
fixes.fix: Append to reading 1 answers: "They take Psalm 51:5 as the psalmist's own confession of a sinfulness he shares with all people, and not as guilt contracted at conception." Append to reading 3 answers: "They take Psalm 51:5 as the psalmist's words about his own sin and the sin all people share."

fixes.why: The summary says Anglican members hold parts of reading 1, but Anglican is not in its held_by while it is in readings 2 and 3, so the page contradicts itself.
fixes.fix: Either add "Anglican" to reading 1's held_by, or change the last sentence to "Some members of other traditions hold parts of this reading." The second is shorter and avoids a three-way Anglican placement.

fixes.why: The card calls these Christian terms but never says they are later names given to readings of the text, not words of the Bible. A scholar will want the origin stated so the reader does not take the label as the Bible's own. Also, 'regeneration' has a Berean-visible sense (Titus 3:5, 'the washing of new birth') that the note leaves out.
fixes.fix: total depravity: "The Reformed name, from the seventeenth century, for ..." (the rest unchanged). original sin: add "The term is not in the Bible; it names a reading of Romans 5:12 and related verses that Christians have held since the early church."

fixes.why: The agreed block and intro say 'the text says' as if the whole Bible spoke with one voice. The card does not mention that these are Christian readings of texts written in different periods (Genesis, Psalms, Paul), and the Jewish and other non-Christian readings are absent. This is a limit, not a tilt, and should be stated.
fixes.fix: Add a closing sentence to the intro: "These are Christian readings; the Hebrew Scriptures cited here are read differently in Jewish tradition, which does not hold inherited sin."

summary: Every quote is the Berean's exact words, no verdict words were found, and the three readings are even in count and stated in their holders' terms. The fixes put the Lutheran and Reformed proof text for inherited sin (Ephesians 2:3) where they would look for it, give the Catholic and Orthodox reading a verse for the will, and mark the allegorical, later-named and Christian-only status of what is quoted.
